transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-02-27
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Nina Torres (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (ZenWave Head of Cloud Partnerships), Priya Rao (ZenWave Solutions Architect), Evan Cho (ZenWave CTO), Jules Marin (ZenWave Business Ops)
Links shared: Redwood partner one-pager (link), handoff deck (link), ZenWave staging network diagram (will be shared)

Summary:
Quick partner intro to scope reseller/onramp model and technical requirements for a small pilot (focused on hybrid GPU capacity routing). High-level commercial model discussed (reseller margin, pass-through billing vs committed capacity). Technical topics: API compatibility, private deployment options, VPC peering, VPN and SSO, telemetry and billing attribution. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics:
- Commercial model: margins, committed capacity, credits
- Integration patterns: API onramp vs dedicated routing + edge pooling
- Security/compliance: SOC2, audit logs, KMS, SSO/SAML
- Pilot framing: sample workloads, success criteria, timelines
- Technical open questions: KV cache behavior across routed models, prefix caching, multi-tenant routing, failover policy

Transcript (timestamps approximate, auto-transcribed, some words may be off):
00:00 Maya Patel: Alright everyone thanks for making time, this is Maya with Redwood, I'm gonna kick it off, quick intros - I'll hand it to Liam for the technical bit after I frame the partner go-to-market...
00:18 Carlos Mendez: Hey Maya, thanks, Carlos here. ZenWave's super excited, we run a channel of small cloud providers and resellers, looking to onramp Redwood models for customers that want lower latency regionally and predictable unit economics.
00:35 Priya Rao: Hi all, Priya, I'm our solutions architect, I'll be the tech point.
00:42 Liam O'Connor: Liam from Redwood infra, I look after integrations and performance, happy to deep dive.
00:50 Evan Cho: Evan, CTO, quick note: we care about telemetry and per-tenant cost attribution, so the billing side is important for us.
01:05 Maya Patel: Great, short agenda: 1) commercial & partner motion 2) technical constraints 3) pilot framing 4) next steps. Does that sound okay?
01:12 Jules Marin: Yep sounds good.
01:20 Maya Patel: For commercial, there's two common patterns - reseller pass-through where you bill customers directly and we invoice ZenWave at list minus partner margin; or dedicated committed pools where you reserve capacity and mark up. Curious what aligns with your ops?
01:39 Carlos Mendez: We're lean ops, prefer pass-through initially, but may reserve for very high throughput customers. Question on how usage attribution works though.
01:50 Maya Patel: On the hosted API side we can attach partner tokens and per-customer metadata; the Console gives token-level cost and latency breakdowns. If you want reserved capacity we can do Dedicated with billing reconciliation.
02:05 Priya Rao: Do you support per-tenant RBAC and separate audit logs? Our customers require separate audit trails.
02:14 Nina Torres: We do, you can configure audit log retention and per-route tracing. For Private deployments we support customer-managed audit logs as well.
02:26 Evan Cho: How about KMS integration, can we plug in our HSM?
02:30 Liam O'Connor: Yes, for Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM; for hosted we manage keys but can bring-your-own-key via supported KMS providers.
02:39 Carlos Mendez: Good. On the tech side, Priya has details on routing.
02:45 Priya Rao: Right our flow: we want to route based on region and latency, prefer Redwood to be able to handle fallback to a lower-cost model if capacity constrained. Also need a deterministic cost estimate for units.
03:00 Liam O'Connor: That maps well to our smart routing -- policy-based routing by region/latency/cost tier, with model variant fallback. One caveat: cross-region KV cache sharing is limited so you might see cold starts on failover unless prefix caching is applied.
03:20 Priya Rao: Cold starts are tricky for us; can we pin model variants to certain routes?
03:25 Liam O'Connor: Yes, pinning by model version and region is supported. Also prefix caching and sticky routing can reduce cold starts. Note: our KV cache often referred to as "KV cash" in some transcriptions -- it's KV cache.
03:36 Carlos Mendez: Cool, rough Q on throughput: our typical customer wants 50–200 concurrent streams with bursts. Does Redwood Dedicated map to that?
03:45 Liam O'Connor: Yes Dedicated GPU pools can be sized; autoscaling policies can handle bursts but we recommend a small commit for a baseline. We can share a sizing guideline.
04:00 Maya Patel: On SLAs, Dedicated comes with an SLA for uptime and latency tiers, Hosted is best effort but very reliable for normal usage.
04:12 Evan Cho: Ok can you share the SLA doc?
04:15 Maya Patel: Yep, will share.
04:22 Jules Marin: Security checklist: SOC2, ISO, SSO support?
04:25 Nina Torres: We are SOC2 compliant, we have ISO documentation in the partner pack, and we support SAML/SSO and SCIM provisioning.
04:35 Carlos Mendez: Great. A couple of integration specifics we often get asked: do you support private VPC peering or do customers need VPN?
04:45 Liam O'Connor: Both are options. Hosted supports IP allowlists and private link depending on cloud. Private deployment can be in your VPC. For cross account we support VPC peering and/or customer-managed VPN.
04:58 Priya Rao: Latency budgets: we need 75th percentile under 120ms for short prompts in our region. Any notes?
05:06 Liam O'Connor: We can hit that in most cases; depends on model and sequence length. We'll suggest model variant selection and batching configs to meet that SLO. We'll capture sample prompts to validate.
05:20 Maya Patel: Quick commercial Q: what's your expected timeline for pilot?
05:24 Carlos Mendez: We're targeting mid March to show to two channel customers by April. Hope to have technical check done early March.
05:33 Maya Patel: Sounds reasonable. We'll aim for the compatibility matrix in first week of March.
05:40 (crosstalk)
06:05 Priya Rao: On the API, do you expose token-level logs we can pull into our billing system or do we need to use the Console export?
06:13 Nina Torres: We have APIs to pull usage events and token breakdowns; also scheduled exports for S3 if you'd rather ingest to your BI.
06:23 Evan Cho: For pilot we need a simple way to tag tenant traffic so that it's clear which channel customer generated tokens. How does tagging work?
06:31 Liam O'Connor: You can use partner-scoped API keys with metadata tags on request. Console and APIs both surface these tags for attribution.
06:40 Carlos Mendez: Any known limitations re: quantized models when used across dedicated/dedicated-on-edge?
06:47 Liam O'Connor: Quantization profiles vary by hardware, and we do kernel selection per instance. You might see slight quality variance — Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles per workload. We'll run a small eval.
07:00 Priya Rao: Are there any extra software agents we need to run on our side?
07:05 Liam O'Connor: No agent is required for hosted usage. For Private deployments there's an installer and a small runtime which we provide; that's what you'd deploy into your VPC or air-gapped env.
07:16 Carlos Mendez: Ok can you also speak to multi-tenant isolation? A few customers ask for strict compute isolation.
07:25 Nina Torres: Dedicated pools provide isolation at the GPU pool level. For strictest isolation we'd recommend private deployment or dedicated single-tenant pools.
07:35 Jules Marin: Contracting question: minimum term for dedicated reserve?
07:40 Maya Patel: Typical starts at 3 months for short pilots, then 12-month for committed discounts. We'll include contract language examples.
07:50 Carlos Mendez: Sweet.
08:05 (longer section where Liam shares a screen; auto-transcript degrades)
28:12 Liam O'Connor: ...so you can see routing policy here, you create a rule that says prefer region A up to 80% load, fallback to region B at 100ms threshold, and otherwise fall back to the cheaper model variant.
28:34 Priya Rao: I see, when a fallback happens do you preserve KV cache keys or is it a new state?
28:40 Liam O'Connor: New state — cross-region cache coherence for KV cache isn't synchronized, so unless you warm the prefix you may hit cold context. We can mitigate with prefix replication for some cases but it's not global.
28:55 Carlos Mendez: Will that hit our latency budgets if we see a failover?
29:02 Liam O'Connor: Potentially for a short window. That's why sticky routing or pinning is recommended for latency-sensitive flows.
29:15 Priya Rao: Noted.
30:05 Maya Patel: Alright let's frame the pilot: objective — validate routing and attribution for two channel customers. Success criteria — 1) <120ms p75 for short prompts for region A 2) correct billing attribution to ZenWave tokens 3) smoke test with 100 concurrent streams. We'd propose a 2-week tech validation then a 4-week pilot. Thoughts?
30:35 Carlos Mendez: That sounds good. Quick ask: can you supply a simple test plan we can run?
30:41 Liam O'Connor: Yes, we'll send a compatibility test matrix and a step-by-step plan.
30:47 Maya Patel: Next on legal, any compliance hoops for channel reselling we should know?
30:53 Jules Marin: We need demonstration of data residency and audit logs for our customers in EU.
31:00 Nina Torres: We'll include EU region options and log retention docs.
31:12 Evan Cho: Are there pricing tiers for embedding calls vs generation?
31:17 Maya Patel: Yes embeddings are priced differently; we'll include the detailed pricing sheet. Also note tokens/embedding unit definitions in the brief.
31:30 Priya Rao: One more technical note — some customers use GPU endpoints with NVLink and expect large context performance, is Redwood optimized for that config?
31:42 Liam O'Connor: Our serving runtime supports NVLink-aware kernels and large KV caches on nodes with fast interconnect. We'll confirm mapping to your hardware profiles.
31:55 (short pause)
32:10 Carlos Mendez: On go-to-market, we want joint collateral, a short integration guide, and a co-branded page. Is that doable?
32:18 Maya Patel: Absolutely, we have partner co-marketing kits and can do a technical joint playbook.
32:26 Maya Patel: I'll recap next steps — send the partner brief, SLA, test matrix; Liam will run compatibility tests; ZenWave shares infra diagrams and stakeholder list; target pilot kickoff mid March.
32:40 Carlos Mendez: Thanks, appreciate the quick follow up.
32:50 Maya Patel: Anything else from ZenWave?
32:55 Priya Rao: No, looking forward.
33:00 Evan Cho: No, thanks everyone.
33:10 Maya Patel: Great. We'll meet again after the test runs.
33:20 (call ends)

Note about transcription: speaker labels and timestamps are approximate; occasional mis-hearings (eg "KV cash" instead of KV cache, "prefixing" vs "prefix caching") are present.

End of transcript.
